screen1-a1.where: Top left, three horizontal lines next to the word messenger.
screen1-a1.expectation: It opens a side menu with the other sections of the app.
screen1-a1.cue: The three-line picture. That is the standard menu glyph.

first_pass.why: Three stacked lines is the menu icon on nearly every app I use.

screen1-a2.where: Top right, a square with a pencil going into it.
screen1-a2.cue: The pencil on a square. In a messaging app a pencil usually means write a new one.

first_pass.why: A pencil means 'write' or 'edit'. I think it is a new message, but it could also mean 'edit this list'. There is no word on it.
first_pass.solution: Put the words 'New message' next to the pencil.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "A pencil means 'write' or 'edit'. I think it is a new message, but it could also mean 'edit this list'. There is no word on it." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a2 (Top right, a square with a pencil going into it.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "It starts a new message."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: On the live Chats screen I pressed the square with the pencil. After a moment a screen titled 'New message' opened, with 'To: Type a name or group', and rows 'New story', 'New note' and 'Group chat' under it. I came back with the arrow at the top left.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: It does start a new message, and the screen it opens names itself. The pencil still has no word on it, so I only know this because I pressed it.

screen1-a3.where: Top right corner, a black circle with a white letter f.
screen1-a3.expectation: It probably opens the Facebook app.

first_pass.why: A logo is a brand, not an action. I do not know if it opens Facebook, switches account, or shows Facebook content inside this app. If it takes me out of this app without warning, that is a problem for me.
first_pass.solution: Text that says exactly what happens, for example 'Open Facebook'.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "A logo is a brand, not an action. I do not know if it opens Facebook, switches account, or shows Facebook content inside this app. If it takes me out of this..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a3 (Top right corner, a black circle with a white letter f.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "It probably opens the Facebook app."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the black circle with the white 'f'. Messenger disappeared and the Facebook app opened on its own Notifications page, showing friend suggestions and 'Add friend' / 'Remove' buttons. Nothing warned me I was leaving Messenger. The phone's Back button kept me inside Facebook on its home feed, so I had to open Messenger again myself.

screen1-a3.closing_comment: It is worse than I thought. It throws me into a different app without saying so, and Back does not bring me back.

screen1-a4.where: Blue bar under the header: 'Notifications are currently off. Tap to turn on.'
screen1-a4.expectation: It turns notifications on, or takes me to the setting for it.
screen1-a4.cue: The text says it: 'Tap to turn on.'

first_pass.why: The sentence is literal and says what tapping does.

screen1-a5.where: Grey rounded box with a magnifying glass: 'Ask Meta AI or search'.
screen1-a5.expectation: I type a name to search my chats, or I type a question to an AI.
screen1-a5.cue: The magnifying glass and the placeholder 'Ask Meta AI or search'.

first_pass.why: It is two different things in one box. When I type a name I do not know if it searches my contacts or sends my words to the AI. I want to know which before I type.
first_pass.solution: Separate search from the AI, or show which one will run before I submit.

test_cases.targets: the thing you said made it hard: "It is two different things in one box. When I type a name I do not know if it searches my contacts or sends my words to the AI. I want to know which before I..." - does trying it on the phone settle what it is for?
test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); tap the box tagged a5 (Grey rounded box with a magnifying glass: 'Ask Meta AI or search'.), type something you would really put there, watch the screen while you type, then delete what you typed without sending anything
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: while you type you can no longer tell what the box is for, or it does not take what you expected (you said: "I type a name to search my chats, or I type a question to an AI.")
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: the screen keeps showing what the box is for and it takes what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I tapped the 'Ask Meta AI or search' box on the Chats screen. A search screen opened with a 'Suggested' list of people. I typed 'Deki'. Results appeared straight away: Deki 'Connected', then 'More people' and filter tabs 'All, People, Messages, Groups, Pages'. A separate pill button 'Ask' with the purple dots appeared at the right end of the box. I deleted my text and went back with the arrow. Nothing was sent.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: Typing searches. The AI is a separate 'Ask' button that only shows up once I type. The empty box still says both things, so I have to start typing before I find out.

screen1-a6.expectation: It lets me write a short status note.
screen1-a6.cue: The words 'Drop a thought' in a speech bubble.

first_pass.why: 'Drop a thought' is a figure of speech. I do not drop thoughts. I am guessing it means post a short note.
first_pass.solution: Literal text: 'Write a note'.

test_cases.action: go to the first screen the app opens on (the list with the word 'messenger' at the top and 'Chats', 'People', 'Notifications' at the bottom); press the box tagged a6 (Top half of the first column of faces: a speech bubble 'Drop a thought' over a grey silhouette.), look at what appears, then come back with the arrow at the top left or the phone's Back.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected (you said: "It lets me write a short status note."), or you still cannot tell what it did
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears matches what you expected and you can tell what it did
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the speech bubble over the grey person on the Chats screen. A screen titled 'New note' opened, with a 'Share a thought...' bubble, the keyboard, and the line 'Anyone can see your note on Messenger and Facebook for 24 hours.' I closed it with the X without writing anything. During this session the same bubble on the Chats screen said 'What's up?', then 'Share a song', then 'Post a note...', then 'What's up?' again.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: Pressing it confirms it means 'write a note'. But the label is never literal and keeps changing by itself, so I still cannot rely on it before I press.
